summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~76% YoY to ~Rs 2,725 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to ~4% (from 5.8%), with EBITDA ~Rs 110 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was about Rs 2,725 crore, up ~76% YoY, with EBITDA of about Rs 110 crore (+22% YoY) and PAT of about Rs 69 crore (+23% YoY). EBITDA margin compressed to ~4% from 5.8% a year earlier, though up ~48 bps from Q4 FY26's 3.5%, which management attributed to product mix and the ramp-up of value-added copper. The copper anode line was fully commissioned, with ~600 tonnes sold since commissioning, and Unit-2 restarted on 27 July 2026 after a furnace accident on 14 July. Management gave no quantitative volume or margin guidance beyond directional statements that FY27 margins and EBITDA per tonne should improve.

segments.name: Copper and copper products
segments.commentary: Now ~67% of revenue. Anode line runs at 1,600 MT/month installed capacity after both furnaces started; ~600 MT anode sold in the quarter. Management cited copper EBITDA of ~Rs 31,000-32,000/tonne in Q1 vs ~Rs 36,000/tonne FY26 average and ~Rs 13,000 in Q4 FY26 (as stated in Q&A).

segments.name: Lead and lead alloy
segments.commentary: ~29% of revenue. Management said margins fell from ~7-7.5% toward lower levels due to expensive raw material from West Asia disruption; capacity expansion of 15-20% over ~1,85,000 tonnes (FY26 volume) is awaiting approval.

segments.name: Aluminium and alloys
segments.commentary: ~3% of revenue; no further commentary in the call.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 copper EBITDA/tonne and overall margins to improve as value-added products ramp up; it cited an average uplift of ~2% (around Rs 25/tonne per Q&A) on value-added volumes at steady state.
Copper cathode Phase-1 (1,500 MT/month installed) targeted for Q2 FY27; a 750 MT cathode facility to begin volumes about a month after readiness.
Copper wire rod (600 MT/month) and copper busbar and profiles (1,500 MT/month) targeted for Q3 FY27.
Antimony project (1,000 MT lead antimony bullion, ~100 MT/month output) on schedule for Q3 FY27; Ahmedabad JV trial production started, stabilisation expected in Q2 FY27.
Plastic recycling facility (~Rs 15 crore, ~6 acres) targeted for Q3 FY27; Kuwait investment expected to contribute from Q3 FY27 subject to shipping normalisation.
FY27 capex outlay of ~Rs 87 crore, mainly copper value-added, antimony and plastic recycling.
No quantitative revenue, volume or EBITDA guidance given; management declined to guide FY27/FY28 volume growth percentages.
capex_capacity: Copper anode line commissioned in Q1 FY27; installed capacity 1,600 MT/month with both furnaces operational.
Copper cathode: civil construction complete; Phase-1 of 1,500 MT/month installed capacity for Q2 FY27.
Copper wire rod 600 MT/month and busbar/profiles 1,500 MT/month, both for Q3 FY27.
Ahmedabad JV with C&Y Group: designed for ~72,000 tonnes/year copper-bearing scrap and ~25,000 tonnes/year copper products at full ramp-up; trial production started.

Unit-2 (Gummidipoondi) furnace shed resumed operations after approval on 27 July 2026 following the 14 July furnace accident (one contract worker died, others injured); insurance claim under settlement. Management said the one-week closure would not affect annual production.
demand_pricing: Management said the West Asia conflict caused raw material shortages, forcing purchases of expensive local and imported material, which pressured lead margins.
Around Rs 20-30 crore of raw material remains stuck on a vessel at Dubai port; management said it is insured against war risk.

Regulatory tailwind: amended hazardous waste rules require manufacturers of cables, conductors and similar products to collect end-of-life items and use recycled copper/aluminium/zinc at 5% from FY28, rising to 10% later. Management said the volume impact is hard to quantify.
Most new copper value-added customers are expected to be new to the company, with in-principle go-aheads received from many.
Management said competition is welcome and the regulation applies to all players.

qa_highlights.question: How will lead and copper EBITDA margins move over the next three quarters and full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamlesh Jain attributed lead margin pressure to West Asia raw material costs and said copper value-added products should offset it; he expects a better FY27 margin but gave no figures. Hemant Jain said EBITDA per tonne, not percentage margin, is the right metric.

qa_highlights.question: What volume guidance is there for lead and copper in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there would be some volume growth in later FY27 but declined to give percentages, calling it premature. Lead capacity expansion of 15-20% is pending approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the furnace incident on volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one-week closure and maintenance shutdown would have no material impact on production, given spare capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 FY26 copper EBITDA/tonne so low (~Rs 13,000), and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business should be viewed on a two-quarter average because of hedging and the procurement-to-sale cycle; Q1 copper margin was back to normal. Value-added copper is expected to add ~Rs 25/tonne at stabilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is raw material still 100% hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamlesh Jain said the 100% hedging policy is unchanged, that hedging is a cost centre and not a speculative position, and that broker limits exceed $30 million.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategic rationale for the telecom infrastructure diversification?
qa_highlights.answer: Mayank Pareek said the company already removes redundant copper cables for telecom firms and has added a new object clause to lay optical fibre cable as an incidental activity. No revenue or margin numbers were given.

risks_watch: Lead margins under pressure from expensive West Asia raw material; management gave no lead EBITDA/tonne figure and no lead volume guidance, only 15-20% capacity expansion pending approval.

Copper EBITDA/tonne volatility: management cited ~Rs 13,000/tonne in Q4 FY26 versus ~Rs 31,000-32,000 in Q1 FY27 and ~Rs 36,000 FY26 average; value-added uplift of ~Rs 25/tonne only at stabilisation, timing unspecified.
Rs 20-30 crore of raw material stuck on a vessel at Dubai port, stated as war-risk insured; release timing uncertain; Kuwait machinery dispatch and Q3 FY27 start depend on shipping normalisation.

Execution risk on copper cathode (Q2 FY27), wire rod, busbar and profiles, antimony and plastic recycling (Q3 FY27), and Ahmedabad JV stabilisation (Q2 FY27); anode ramp from current volumes to 1,600 MT/month installed.
Unit-2 furnace shed restart after the 14 July 2026 accident; insurance claim under settlement, amount not disclosed; safety and compliance scrutiny.
Regulatory tailwind from hazardous waste rule (5% recycled content from FY28, 10% later) is unquantified by management; telecom optical-fibre diversification has no revenue or margin figures yet.

So, it is premature to talk now on how much EBITDA we are going to expect in this all the expansion get over.

summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term copper value-added story and the regulatory tailwind, but cautious and evasive on numbers: management repeatedly declined to give FY27/FY28 volume, revenue, EBITDA or margin guidance, citing business nature and external disruptions. Defensive when challenged on the Q4 FY26 copper margin and on hedging, asserting that the two-quarter average is the right lens.
